raw_case_text:
A 19-year-old male patient was referred to the emergency department with seizure. He had a history of fever and generalized weakness about 2 weeks before. According to having the history of consuming continuously dairy products made from unpasteurized milk, the serologic Brucella tests including wright, 2ME, and coombs wright were checked. Serum SAT test was positive at titer of 1/1,280, and with the diagnosis of brucellosis, the doxycycline and streptomycin were prescribed for him since about 2 weeks before admission. Two weeks later, the patient referred to our hospital with seizure. Convulsion was generalized, tonic, and colonic lasting about 5 min. He had no history of recent drug usage (except for treatment of brucellosis), alcohol consumption, and smoking. No history of head trauma was declared. Vital signs and general examination were not remarkable. He was afebrile. Complete blood cell count was in normal limits. HBS-Ag, HCV-Ab, HIV test, and serum toxic panel were all negative.
Brain computed tomography scan was performed, which was with no abnormality. The lumbar puncture (LP) was performed. Cerebral spinal fluid (CSF) revealed no abnormality; it was colorless and clear; glucose = 67, protein = 15 mg/dL, red blood cell = 0, and white blood cell = 0. The CSF was also sent for Brucella and herpes simplex (HSV 1 and 2) polymerase chain reaction (PCR) studies. Status epilepticus was defined, and patient required intubation and mechanical ventilation. Antiepileptic drugs were started. According to brucellosis, with the clinical suspicious for neurobrucellosis, the treatment including ceftriaxone 2 g every 12 h intravenous (IV), doxycycline 100 mg every 12 h, and rifampin 600 mg daily in addition to IV acyclovir were started. In ICU, the clinical seizure classification was focal and lateralizing signs were right facial and arm clonic and right versive. The electroencephalography monitoring was performed, and the midazolam infusion was started. Brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and magnetic resonance venography (MRV) were both normal. CSF PCR studies for Brucella and HSV, 1 and 2, were reported negative and CSF adenosine deaminase reported 10. Serologic test for brucellosis on CSF were negative. With the probable diagnosis of neurobrucellosis, the treatment with ceftriaxone, doxycycline, and rifampin were continued. Also, 14-day course of IV acyclovir was completed. After 1 month, the patient was stable and treatment with oral doxycycline, rifampin, and co-trimuxazole accompanied with antiepileptic drugs were continued. Two weeks after discharge the patient readmitted to hospital with status epilepticus and was intubated again. The LP was performed, which revealed normal CSF analysis. HSV, 1 and 2, PCR in addition to Brucella PCR were negative in CSF again. The patient underwent renewed brain MRI and MRV and both were normal. Extensive workup did not reveal any cause of the symptoms; however, NMDAR antibodies were positive in both serum and CSF; hence, the diagnosis of NMDAR encephalitis was established. He was started on IV methylprednisolone, which yielded limited improvement. According to intractable epilepsy, the patient's treatment consisting of plasmapheresis and intravenous immunoglobulin was started.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 19-year-old male presented to the emergency department with a new-onset generalized tonic-clonic seizure.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient presented with a 5-minute generalized tonic-clonic seizure following a 2-week history of fever and generalized weakness. Two weeks prior to admission, he had been evaluated for systemic febrile illness and commenced on antimicrobial therapy. In the emergency department, he progressed into refractory status epilepticus requiring endotracheal intubation, mechanical ventilation, and continuous intravenous midazolam infusion. Following initial stabilization and discharge, he was readmitted two weeks later with recurrent status epilepticus.
subjective.past_medical_history: Prior diagnosis of systemic febrile illness treated with doxycycline and streptomycin for 2 weeks prior to presentation. Denied alcohol use, tobacco smoking, or head trauma. Epidemiological exposure: continuous consumption of dairy products made from unpasteurized milk.
subjective.review_of_systems: Generalized tonic-clonic convulsion, prior fever and generalized weakness. Denied toxic ingestions. Home medications: doxycycline and streptomycin. Allergies: not documented.

objective.physical_examination: Afebrile; vital signs and general physical examination were unremarkable. ICU neurological exam: focal motor seizures with lateralizing features (right facial and right upper limb clonic jerks, right versive head turning); comatose requiring mechanical ventilation.
objective.routine_investigations: Complete blood count: within normal limits. Infectious and toxicologic screening: HBsAg, HCV Ab, HIV test, and urine/serum toxicological panel were all negative. Continuous electroencephalography (EEG): documented status epilepticus.
objective.advanced_workup: Brain CT without contrast: normal. Initial and repeat lumbar puncture: colorless, clear CSF with glucose 67 mg/dL, protein 15 mg/dL, RBC 0/cumm, WBC 0/cumm, and adenosine deaminase (ADA) 10 U/L. Initial and repeat CSF PCR for HSV types 1 and 2 and targeted zoonotic bacterial PCR in CSF were negative. CSF agglutination serology was negative. Initial and repeat brain MRI and magnetic resonance venography (MRV): normal.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation:
Definitive diagnosis: Anti-NMDA receptor (NMDAR) autoimmune encephalitis triggered in the setting of concurrent/preceding systemic brucellosis. Systemic brucellosis confirmed by positive serum standard agglutination test (SAT) at 1 : 1,280 titer, positive 2-mercaptoethanol (2-ME), and positive Coombs Wright. Direct central nervous system neurobrucellosis was ruled out by negative CSF Brucella PCR, negative CSF serology, normal CSF biochemistry, absent CSF pleocytosis, and normal brain MRI/MRV; HSV 1/2 encephalitis was excluded by negative CSF PCR. Anti-NMDAR encephalitis was confirmed by positive anti-NMDA receptor antibodies in both serum and CSF.
Plan & Outcome: Received empirical neurobrucellosis coverage with IV ceftriaxone (2 g every 12h), oral doxycycline (100 mg every 12h), oral rifampin (600 mg daily), cotrimoxazole, and a 14-day course of IV acyclovir alongside antiepileptic therapy (midazolam infusion). Following readmission for recurrent status epilepticus and autoimmune confirmation, he was treated with IV methylprednisolone, therapeutic plasma exchange (plasmapheresis), and intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG).
